apps.localizedDescription:
Just Volleyball - iOS build:

Godot 4.7.2 project plus a GitHub Actions pipeline that produces an unsigned .ipa on GitHub's macOS runners. You do not need a Mac and you do not need an Apple Developer account to get the file; you only need an Apple ID on the device to sign it at install time.

• Fallback: the same file is attached to every run under Actions -> iOS -> Artifacts (just-volleyball-unsigned-ipa), for 90 days.
• Target: iOS 15+, iPhone and iPad, landscape only.
• Device requirement: A12 or newer (iPhone XS/XR and later, any current iPad). Godot's Metal renderer declares the iphone-ipad-minimum-performance-a12 capability, so older devices will refuse to install it.

versions.localizedDescription:
All six complaints were real, and each one is fixed at the cause:

• Replays: tap to skip. The skip was read from the accept key, which a phone has no way to press, so the vote could not be cast there at all. Any tap during a replay now casts it, and the banner names the gesture the device actually has ("tap to skip" on a phone, "space to skip" on a desktop). A tap also pauses and resumes inside the replay viewer.
• Round movement wheel. The wheel's base was built with its corner radius at the default of 0, which draws square corners, so the circular stick sat on a flat card. It is now the same disc as its rim and knob, and the "move" label is gone.
• No more frozen yellow. The yellow slab is the transition cover, and the next scene used to be loaded synchronously underneath it: the loading thread is the main thread, so the cover could not animate and a big venue read as a hang. Scenes now load on a worker thread while the cover runs a progress bar, the sweeps are shorter (about 0.33 s in, 0.2 s out), and the cover holds until the incoming scene has actually drawn - the first look at a new screen is a finished one, not a half-built court. The boot intro is about half as long and no longer waits out the full audio sting after its animation has finished.
• Exit really exits. SceneTree.quit() only stops the main loop, and iOS answers it by leaving the app alive on its last frame - that is exactly what an exit button that "freezes for a second instead of closing" is. Saving happens first, then the process is ended, on every exit path (menu confirm, pause menu, launch gate).
• Real saving. Settings, profile and career are flushed when the app is backgrounded (NOTIFICATION_APPLICATION_PAUSED is the only leaving notice a phone gives, and a suspended app can be killed without another word) and before quitting. Progress no longer depends on the 2-minute autosave.
• Easier to start. A touch device that has never been asked starts on the easy CPU preset with aim assist on - a phone has no keyboard and no mouse, so the desktop defaults were the wrong starting point. It happens exactly once, never overrides a deliberate choice (the choice flag is persisted), and both stay ordinary settings you can change.

Not verified by me:

Nothing here was checked on a phone - I have no iOS device. What was verified on the exact released file: the sha256 matches the published .sha256, the headless gate below ran green in CI before the export, and the pack audit passes inside the IPA.

Harmless notes:

• The difficulty/aim-assist preset applies once and never again: if you set a difficulty yourself, that wins forever.
• The gate (tools/verify_transitions.gd) is a headless regression test that CI runs before every export; it caught two real bugs while being written. It runs without a device, so on-device times (how long a venue actually takes now) are still yours to confirm.
• A12 or newer, unsigned, same install method: Sideloadly / AltStore as before.
